subject.title: [Bug]: Block streaming can drop paragraph separators across streamed updates

question: Should the permanent fix use one of the open in-band separator-preservation PRs, or should block streaming first carry explicit paragraph/newline/hard-split boundary metadata?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but the durable boundary contract affects shared streamed delivery semantics and two open PRs already propose the narrower text-based fix shape.

options.title: Consolidate one separator-preserving PR
options.body: Review one linked PR as the canonical fix, require chunker reconstruction and coalescer no-double-separator coverage including maxChars boundaries, and close the other PR as superseded after choosing the viable path.

options.title: Require boundary metadata first
options.body: Pause the linked text-based PRs until a metadata-carrying separator contract is designed and tested through chunking, coalescing, and delivery.

options.title: Reject the current direction
options.body: Close or redirect the linked PRs and leave this issue open for a maintainer-sponsored redesign of streaming boundary semantics.

recommendation.title: Consolidate one separator-preserving PR
recommendation.body: Review one linked PR as the canonical fix, require chunker reconstruction and coalescer no-double-separator coverage including maxChars boundaries, and close the other PR as superseded after choosing the viable path.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged paragraph/newline block-streaming work is the clearest origin of the current boundary contract.
